requirements.text: Limit on future routine GP appointments: A patient shall not hold more than two future routine GP appointments at the same time across all sites. Nurse reviews, immunisations and physiotherapy are excluded from this limit.
Minimum lead time for online booking: The portal shall not allow a booking that starts less than two hours from the current time.

Childhood immunisation booking by carers within age range: Childhood immunisation appointments shall only be bookable by a carer for a dependant whose age is within the range set for that immunisation type in the PMS.

Free-text reason for appointment: Before confirming a booking, the portal shall ask the patient for a free-text reason for the appointment of up to 200 characters and pass it to the PMS with the booking.
Notice that reason field is unmonitored: The portal shall tell patients that the reason field is not monitored and that urgent problems must be telephoned in.

Urgent-problem warning on every booking screen: The portal shall show a warning on every booking screen that it must not be used for urgent medical problems, with the clinic telephone number and the national urgent care number.
Booking confirmed only after PMS acceptance: The portal shall write a confirmed booking to the PMS and show the patient a confirmation only after the PMS has accepted it.
Patient cancellation up to two hours before start: A patient shall be able to cancel an appointment through the portal up to two hours before its start time.
Move appointment to another slot of same type: A patient shall be able to move an appointment to another slot of the same appointment type.
Release original slot only after new booking accepted: When an appointment is moved, the original slot shall be released only after the PMS has accepted the new booking.
Cancellation reason from managed list: The portal shall ask a cancelling patient to choose a reason from a list maintained by the practice managers.
Telephone bookings visible and cancellable in portal: Appointments booked by telephone shall be visible in the portal and cancellable by the patient in the same way as online bookings.
No local copy of appointment book: The portal shall not keep its own copy of the appointment book; every availability search and booking shall be made against the PMS.
Receptionist view of portal account status: Receptionists shall be able to see, for any patient, whether the patient has a portal account and whether it is locked.

Per-site online bookability of appointment types: Practice managers shall be able to mark or unmark each appointment type at their own site as bookable online, with the change taking effect in the portal within fifteen minutes.

Daily front-desk list of online activity: Front-desk staff shall be able to see a list of the day's online bookings, cancellations and waiting list offers for their site, including each patient's reason for appointment.
Suspend online booking per clinician for date range: Front-desk staff shall be able to suspend online booking for a single clinician for a date range without changing the PMS rota.

Monthly per-site activity report: The portal shall provide a monthly report per site showing appointments booked, moved and cancelled online, reminders sent, and missed appointments for online and telephone bookings separately.
Urgent and same-day appointments telephone-only in first release: Urgent and same-day appointments shall remain telephone-only in the first release.
No symptom checker or clinical advice: The portal shall not offer a symptom checker or any form of clinical advice.
Automatic offer of cancelled slots to waiting-list patients: A cancelled slot shall be offered automatically to waiting-list patients who said they could attend at that time.

requirements.text: Register claim from multiple channels: The application shall allow a handler to register a claim from an email, a telephone note, or a completed claim form, and record the channel and the date and time the claim was first notified.

Mandatory consignment note number and tracking data retrieval: The application shall require the consignment note number when a claim is registered and retrieve consignment details (collection and delivery dates, depots, exceptions, proof of delivery) from the operational tracking system.
Register claim with unverified consignment: If the consignment note number is not found in the tracking system, the application shall allow registration with the consignment marked as unverified.
Block payment until consignment verified: The application shall prevent any payment on a claim until its consignment has been verified.
Duplicate claim warning: The application shall warn the handler when a new claim is registered for a consignment that already has an open or closed claim, and shall show the existing claim.

Multi-consignment claims with per-consignment loss detail: A single claim shall be able to cover several consignments for the same claimant, with loss type and amount claimed recorded separately for each consignment.

Calculate limit of liability by weight: The application shall calculate the limit of liability for each consignment from the weight of goods lost or damaged and the per-kilogram limit in the claimant's terms.

Declared value overrides per-kilogram limit: Where the claimant declared a value and paid the declared value charge, the limit of liability shall be the declared value instead of the per-kilogram limit.
Special terms take precedence: Where special terms apply, the application shall use the limits in the special terms.
Manager approval for limit override: A handler shall not be able to override the calculated limit of liability without the approval of the claims operations manager.
Amount payable calculation: The amount payable for a consignment shall be the lower of the proven value of the loss and the limit of liability, less any salvage value recovered.

Step-by-step calculation explanation: The application shall show the handler a step-by-step explanation of how the amount payable was calculated, and include the same explanation in the settlement letter.
Exclude consequential losses unless special terms allow: The application shall prevent a handler from including consequential losses in the amount payable unless special terms allow them.
Availability during claims desk hours: The application shall be available at least 99.5% of the time during claims desk working hours, 7am to 7pm on working days.
Concurrent user capacity and page load time: The application shall support at least 40 concurrent users without any page taking more than three seconds to load.
Remote working via standard remote access: The application shall be usable by handlers working from home through the company's standard remote access arrangements.
Reduce average claim settlement time to 30 days: The business goal is to reduce the average time to settle a claim to 30 days within the first year after go-live.
Produce quarterly insurance claim in under a day: The application shall produce the quarterly insurance claim in under a day.
Proactive customer status updates: The application shall send customers proactive status updates at each stage of their claim.

requirements.text: Support all seven grant programmes across the full grant lifecycle: The system shall support all seven grant programmes and the full grant lifecycle, from programme and round set-up through to closure.
Single council record of applicants and grants: The system shall hold the council's record of every applicant organisation and every grant.
Instruct payments without making them: The system shall instruct payments but shall not make them; the finance system remains the system of record for payments.
Finance system integration for payment instructions: The system depends on the council's finance system to execute payments and hold the payment record.
Programme-specific rules isolation: The system shall allow programme-specific rules to be applied to one programme without affecting other programmes.
One record per funded organisation, independent of users: The system shall hold one record per funded organisation, independent of any single user.

Organisation registration with connected people: A person shall be able to register an organisation by providing its name, address, legal form, charity or company number if any, and details of at least two people connected with it who are not related to each other.

Validate registration numbers against public register: Where a charity or company number is given, the system shall check it against the public register and show the officer any difference in registered name and address.

Prevent duplicate organisation registration: The system shall prevent registration of an organisation whose charity or company number is already held on another record and shall direct the person to request access to the existing record.
Multiple users per organisation with peer approval: An organisation record shall support multiple users, and existing users shall approve a new user's request to join.

Officer-assisted user addition when no approver exists: If an organisation has no remaining users able to approve a request, a grants officer shall be able to add a user after verifying the person's connection with the organisation.

Generate grant agreement from programme template: When a grant is approved, the system shall generate a grant agreement from the programme template including amount, purpose, decision-maker conditions, payment schedule and monitoring requirements.
Electronic signature by grant recipient: The grant recipient shall sign the grant agreement electronically through the system.
Two signatories for grants over 5,000: For grants over 5,000 the agreement shall be signed by two people connected with the organisation.
Payment gated on full signature: No payment shall be made on a grant until the agreement has been signed by the recipient and countersigned by the council.
Lapse of unsigned grant offers: An offer of a grant shall lapse if the agreement is not signed within a reasonable time, and the amount shall be returned to the round's budget.
Council staff single sign-on: Council users shall sign in with the council's single sign-on.
External user authentication with second factor: Applicants and external assessors shall sign in with an email address, a password and a second factor.
Redaction of service users' personal data: A grants officer shall be able to remove personal data about applicants' service users from an application without deleting the rest of the application.
Retention of approved grant records for seven years: The system shall retain records of approved grants for seven years after grant closure and then delete them.
Retention of declined applications for two years: The system shall retain records of declined applications for two years after the decision and then delete them.
Optional, segregated equality information: Equality information from applicants shall be optional, stored separately from the application, and not visible to assessors or decision-makers.
Read-only auditor access: Auditors shall have read-only access to the system.
