questions.text: What is the actual date of the steering group meeting, and so the deadline for returning comments? The document is undated and "the end of the month" does not say which month or day.
questions.quote: Comments should be returned to the Patient Access team before the steering group meeting at the end of the month.

questions.text: What is the maximum time between a booking being confirmed and it appearing in the PMS? "Immediately" cannot be tested. Does it match the performance targets in the non-functional section?
questions.quote: The booking appears in the PMS immediately

questions.text: What is the maximum acceptable delay for 'near real time' availability, given that every search is made against the PMS?
questions.quote: Availability shown in the portal shall reflect the PMS appointment book in near real time.

questions.text: Is the availability window fixed at four weeks or configurable, and does it apply to all appointment types, including physiotherapy and travel health? Section 1.4 says only "the next few weeks", and the assumption in section 10 says rotas are held only "at least four weeks ahead". What does the portal show where a site has fewer than four weeks of rota loaded?
questions.quote: The practice managers asked for the window to be short so that clinicians' rotas can still change without moving many booked appointments.

questions.text: Section 1.4 and the shown-appointments rule limit patients to appointment types at their own site, yet physiotherapy follow-ups and travel health are also offered at other sites, and the open issue on cross-site GP booking is undecided. Which sites deliver these services, how are they identified, and if an appointment type is not flagged bookable online at the other site, should its slots still be shown?
questions.quote: the portal shall also offer slots at the other sites that deliver those services.

questions.text: May patients registered at one site book routine GP appointments at another site? The practice managers are split, so who decides and by when? The availability search and booking rules depend on the answer.
questions.quote: Whether patients registered at one site may book routine GP appointments at another site has been discussed but not decided. Two practice managers were in favour and four were against.

questions.text: Is the list of appointment types a committed launch scope or only an expectation? Which types must be configured and tested for go-live?
questions.quote: At launch these are expected to include routine general practitioner consultations, nurse appointments for blood pressure and diabetes reviews, childhood immunisations, travel health consultations and physiotherapy follow-ups.

questions.text: How is 'routine, non-urgent' defined, and who decides whether an appointment type qualifies? Is the bookable-online flag the only control, or is there a rule preventing urgent types from being flagged?
questions.quote: The first release covers routine, non-urgent appointment types that the practice managers have marked as bookable online.

questions.text: What must the 'staff view of online activity' show, which staff roles can use it, and can they act only on their own site? Is the 'day's' list based on appointments made that day or appointments taking place that day, and is it live or periodically refreshed?
questions.quote: a staff view of online activity

questions.text: How does the portal decide that a slot or request is 'urgent' or 'same-day' and so must stay telephone-only (cut-off time or appointment-type flag)? Should the portal direct patients to phone, given that it gives no clinical advice?
questions.quote: Urgent and same-day appointments remain telephone-only in the first release because the clinics triage those calls clinically.

questions.text: What is the inactivity timeout period and the warning lead time? Information governance suggested ten minutes and patient representatives thought this too short. Who decides, and what value is to be built and tested?
questions.quote: The length of the inactivity period after which a session ends has not been agreed. Information governance suggested ten minutes; the patient representatives felt this was too short.

questions.text: Which second-factor mechanism applies on new devices, how is the code delivered, and what happens if the patient has no mobile number or cannot receive the code? questions.quote: the portal shall require a second factor on every sign-in from a device it has not seen before.

questions.quote: A patient shall sign in with an email address and password

questions.quote: using their date of birth, surname, postcode and a one-time code sent to the mobile number held in the PMS

questions.quote: Front-desk staff will not be able to unlock accounts manually in the first release; this was discussed and deliberately left out to avoid creating a social engineering route.

questions.quote: Links for adult dependants, for example a patient with a lasting power of attorney in place, are reviewed periodically.

questions.quote: Front-desk staff are concerned that a slot booked by telephone might still appear free in the portal and be booked twice.

questions.quote: A patient shall not hold more than two future routine GP appointments at the same time across all sites.

questions.text: What happens if due diligence checks fail or are incomplete? Must the system block the application from reaching the decision-maker until the checks are recorded?
questions.quote: A grants officer shall carry out due diligence on every application recommended for funding before it goes to the decision-maker

questions.text: What does 'interest' cover for panel members (financial, personal, family, trustee), and how does the system learn of one: self-declaration or a register check? What happens if exclusion leaves the panel without a quorum or an interest is declared at or after the meeting? Do the same declaration and exclusion rules apply to other decision-makers such as the grants officer, Cabinet member and Cabinet?
questions.quote: A grant panel member who has an interest in an application shall declare it before the panel meets

questions.text: How is the total value determined if a grant is varied or an applicant has linked applications? Does a variation that moves the total across a threshold require re-routing, and does a reduction go to the lower-tier decision-maker?
questions.quote: A variation that changes the amount of the grant shall be decided by the decision-maker who would be required for the new total amount.

questions.text: Is the budget cap a hard block or only a warning, can anyone override it, and does the budget count only approved amounts or also pending ones? What budget applies to Ward Member Grants?
questions.quote: the system shall show the decision-maker the remaining budget before each decision.

questions.text: Does 'over 25,000' for publication refer to the amount approved or requested? Are declined decisions published, is there a publication deadline, and are exemptions available, for example for safeguarding?
questions.quote: Decisions on grants over 25,000 shall be published on the council's website, showing the organisation, the amount and the purpose.

questions.text: Are assessors' comments passed on verbatim or reviewed first, are assessor names withheld, and how are comments handled where moderation changed the score?
questions.quote: declined applicants shall be given the assessors' comments as feedback.

questions.text: How does the system know about members' interests: is the register integrated or maintained manually, and who keeps it current? Does the block cover interests in related organisations?
questions.quote: A ward member shall not be able to recommend a grant to an organisation in which they have declared an interest in the council's register of members' interests.

questions.text: Is there a limit on the size or number of Ward Member Grant recommendations per member or organisation? Is the allocation reserved when a recommendation is made, and what eligibility criteria does the officer check against?
questions.quote: Each ward member shall be able to see their remaining allocation for the year and recommend a grant to an eligible organisation for a project in their ward.

questions.text: What happens to recommendations pending when the six-week pre-election period starts? Does the restriction also stop officer approval and payment, how does the system learn election dates, and does it cover by-elections and all wards or only the ward concerned?
questions.quote: Ward Member Grants shall not be recommended in the six weeks before a local election.

questions.text: Is there a time limit for the officer to approve or reject a recommendation, and what is the decision route under the scheme of delegation for approved Ward Member Grants?
questions.quote: Members recommend grants and an officer checks them before they are paid.

questions.text: What is the specific time limit for signing before an offer lapses, and is it the same for all programmes? The open question in section 16.2 awaits Legal Services advice, so what should the supplier assume until then? Can a lapsed offer be reissued, and who is notified?
questions.quote: if the agreement is not signed within a reasonable time

questions.text: Who counts as 'two people connected with the organisation' (trustees, directors, signatories)? Must they be registered users different from the main contact? Is the 5,000 threshold based on total grant value, and how does it apply to Small Sparks paid via a sponsor?
questions.quote: signed by two people connected with the organisation for grants over 5,000

questions.text: Who is authorised to countersign for the council, does it use the system's electronic signing, and what happens if one party signs but the other does not, or terms change after generation?
questions.quote: countersigned by the council

questions.text: Who decides the instalment amounts and dates for grants over 10,000, and are there rules on the number, size and timing of instalments? How is a grant of exactly 10,000 treated, including after a variation?
questions.quote: grants over 10,000 shall be paid in instalments set out in the payment schedule.

questions.text: Do instalment release conditions apply only to Strategic Partnerships? What must be satisfied before instalments of other programmes' grants over 10,000? Who accepts the monitoring report, by what criteria and timescale, and what happens to the next instalment if the report is late, rejected or unreviewed?
questions.quote: For Strategic Partnerships grants, instalments after the first shall only be released once the previous quarter's monitoring report has been accepted.

questions.text: What counts as payment 'conditions' being met, and how does the system know they are met? The audit found payments made before agreements were signed, so the check must be defined.
questions.quote: When a payment is due under the payment schedule and its conditions have been met

questions.text: What happens when a payment request is rejected by the finance officer, when Finance does not confirm payment, or when the finance system fails it? What happens to a stopped request: who is notified, can it be reinstated, when is registration status checked, and who may override?
questions.quote: A finance officer shall review each payment request and release it to the finance system

questions.text: Where a panel, Cabinet member or Cabinet decides, who is 'the officer who approved the grant' for the segregation rule? Does the restriction also cover officers who assessed or recommended the grant?
questions.quote: the system shall prevent the officer who approved the grant from releasing its payment.

questions.text: Who decides a variation that moves 10% or more between budget items without changing the total? Is the 10% measured per variation or cumulatively, and against the original or the varied amount?
questions.quote: A variation that moves less than 10% of the grant between budget items, without changing the total, shall be decided by a grants officer.

questions.text: Who decides variations that change neither the amount nor the budget allocation, such as more time or a smaller project scale? What are the process steps after a variation is requested: notification, effect on the payment schedule, and re-signing of the amended agreement?
questions.quote: A recipient may need more time, may want to spend money on a different item, or may need to reduce the scale of the project.

questions.text: Is grant size for the reporting bands the total value or the amount after variation, and which band applies if a variation crosses 5,000 or 25,000? When are due dates for mid-point, quarterly and end-of-grant reports set, by whom, and can they change?
questions.quote: Recipients of grants from 5,001 to 25,000 submit a mid-point report and an end-of-grant report.

questions.text: What happens after a report is marked overdue (escalation, withholding payments, clawback)? Are the 14 days calendar or working days? Which users receive reminders and by what channel?
questions.quote: shall mark the report as overdue if it is not submitted within 14 days after the due date.

questions.text: What outcomes of the officer's review exist besides accepted (rejected, returned for revision), what happens when a report is not accepted, and is there a time limit? What counts as evidence of expenditure? How are outcome measures handled for programmes with no round?
questions.quote: record whether it is accepted

questions.text: Is grant closure automatic or done by a user, and which role? What does 'completed' mean for a payment or clawback (paid, received, reconciled, written off)? What happens if the recipient does not repay or the end-of-grant report is never submitted?
questions.quote: every payment and any clawback has been completed

questions.text: Does the 5,000 clawback threshold apply to the amount to be recovered or the original grant value, and does 'over' exclude exactly 5,000? What happens if the programme manager rejects or amends the clawback, and how is 'not used for its agreed purpose' determined and evidenced?
questions.quote: A clawback over 5,000 shall be approved by the programme manager before the request for repayment is sent.

questions.text: Should ward members see only grants in their own ward? How are Strategic Partnerships and other grants covering several wards or none attributed? What level of detail is shown, and are any items restricted where personal data is involved, such as Youth Voice or Winter Warmth?
questions.quote: Each ward member shall be able to see the grants awarded in their ward under all programmes.

questions.text: Which equality information is reported, and how are small numbers handled to avoid identifying individuals? Equality information is optional, kept separately and hidden from assessors, so how long is it retained, who may see it, and in what aggregated form is it used?
questions.quote: by ward and by the equality information applicants provided

questions.text: Which users may run each report, since only ward members and auditors have stated access rules? What performance, export formats and scheduling are required, given reports currently take days?
questions.quote: Officers, members and auditors all need information from the system.

questions.text: Which mobile devices, operating systems and browsers must be supported, and what does 'work on' mean? Does the 30-minute limit cover registration, document upload and bank details or only the form, on which devices, and how will it be tested?
questions.quote: The application process for a grant under 1,000 shall be completable in no more than 30 minutes by a first-time applicant

questions.text: Over what period is the 99.5% availability measured, which hours count, and are planned maintenance windows excluded? How and where is the three-second page load measured, and does the 500-applicant load include uploads and other users such as assessors and officers?
questions.quote: The system shall be available at least 99.5% of the time

questions.text: Which sign-in method applies to council officers acting as assessors, organisation users who are not applicants, auditors, Finance officers and Legal Services? Does single sign-on include a second factor, which second-factor methods are acceptable, and what password rules apply?
questions.quote: applicants and external assessors shall sign in with an email address, a password and a second factor.

questions.text: What happens to records that are neither approved nor declined (withdrawn, ineligible, draft) or approved grants that never close, and when does their retention clock start? Is deletion automatic, and does it apply to backups and Finance records, with exceptions such as legal holds, open audits or clawback?
questions.quote: records of approved grants for seven years after the grant is closed and records of declined applications for two years after the decision

questions.text: The audit record must not be deletable by any user, yet records must be deleted after seven and two years. How do retention rules apply to audit records, and how long must they be kept? Do administrators, supplier support staff and direct database access count as 'any user'?
questions.quote: the audit record shall not be editable or deletable by any user.

questions.text: Should the audit also record events other than changes, such as logins, failed logins, views of sensitive data and exports? How should changes by system processes, integrations or data migration be attributed, and who must be able to search and report on audit records?
questions.quote: Every action that changes a record in the system shall be recorded

questions.text: Six years of records are held but only three financial years are migrated. What happens to the older records, and is that compatible with the aim that reports of funding to an organisation are complete?
questions.quote: Grants made in the three financial years before go-live shall be migrated into the system with their organisation, amount, programme and status, so that reports of funding to an organisation are complete.

questions.text: Does migration include in-progress grants from programmes other than Strategic Partnerships, such as multi-year or part-paid grants, and are their agreements, payment schedules and monitoring reports migrated or only organisation, amount, programme and status?
questions.quote: Strategic Partnerships grants that are in progress at go-live shall be migrated with their agreements, payment schedules and monitoring reports

questions.text: What matching criteria define records that 'appear to refer to the same organisation' (name similarity, number, address, bank details)? What happens to records not merged? How are incomplete source records handled, and what are the migration acceptance criteria and number of loads?
questions.quote: organisation records that appear to refer to the same organisation shall be presented to a grants officer for a decision on whether to merge them.

questions.text: What is the income threshold below which small organisations need not provide accounts? Has the exemption been agreed, does it apply to all programmes, and does it override the due diligence check on accounts and the rule that accounts are uploaded? Who will decide, and by when?
questions.quote: Programme managers have suggested that small organisations with an annual income below a threshold should not have to provide accounts, but the threshold has not been set.

questions.text: Can Youth Voice panel members under 18 take part in decisions recorded in the system, or must an adult record them? If an adult records it, how are the adult's identity and the young person's vote captured for audit? Who decides, and by when?
questions.quote: Legal Services are considering whether they can take part in decisions recorded in the system or whether an adult must record the decision for them.

questions.text: Will ward members be notified when an organisation in their ward applies? If so, what triggers it, how is it delivered, what applicant details may be shared, and who decides by when?
questions.quote: Some ward members have asked to be told when an organisation in their ward applies to any programme; no decision has been made.

questions.text: Which programme-specific rules must the system support for each of the seven programmes? The section says rules are summarised here but the appendix lists them only for some programmes. If a programme's own rules conflict with sections 4 to 12, which takes precedence?
questions.quote: The general requirements in sections 4 to 12 apply to every programme.

questions.text: What does 'without affecting other programmes' mean in testable terms? Must programme rules be configurable by council staff without the supplier, and must changing one programme's rules leave others' behaviour and data unchanged?
questions.quote: The system must allow these rules to be applied for the programme concerned without affecting other programmes.

questions.text: The panel is said to give priority to priority neighbourhoods but the requirement is a score weighting. Is the weighting the only form of priority, who sets its value, and who maintains the neighbourhood list and priority flags? What happens if a project serves several neighbourhoods or only partly serves a priority one?
questions.quote: the fund's panel gives priority to the twelve neighbourhoods identified in the council's deprivation index as being in the most deprived fifth nationally.

questions.text: Should the one-grant-per-year limit be enforced by the system, and at which stage? Can it be overridden, what happens if an organisation succeeds in both spring and autumn rounds, and do declined or withdrawn applications count? Can unspent spring budget carry into the autumn round?
questions.quote: An organisation shall not receive more than one Neighbourhood Fund grant in the same financial year.

questions.text: Should confirmation of funding block the first instalment of year one, which is already budgeted, or only years two and three? What happens if the programme manager does not confirm: is payment blocked, the grant suspended, and who is notified?
questions.quote: the system shall require the programme manager to confirm each year's funding before its first instalment is released.

questions.text: Does the ten working day clock start at submission even if the application is incomplete or the sponsor's bank details are unverified? What happens when the deadline is missed? Who is the decision-maker for Small Sparks under the scheme of delegation, and is ten days compatible with due diligence?
questions.quote: decisions are made within ten working days

questions.text: What does 'much shorter' mean in testable terms, and are registration, eligibility, due diligence and contact details still required for Small Sparks? What criteria define a 'new and very small' group, and does the system check this? Are sponsors optional, are there eligibility conditions or limits on sponsors, and who is liable for clawback and monitoring?
questions.quote: The application form is much shorter than for other programmes and asks only about the activity, the cost and who will benefit.

questions.text: Is the age limit of 16 for youth panel assessors enforced by the system, for example by checking date of birth, and what evidence is recorded and by whom? Is a supporting youth worker mandatory for every youth assessor, and should scoring be blocked if none is recorded?
questions.quote: Assessors for the Youth Voice fund may be members of the youth council aged 16 or over

questions.text: What counts as bad weather, who decides a cancellation was weather-related, and what evidence is required? How are costs already incurred verified and approved, does the system calculate the clawback amount, is partial clawback subject to delegation limits, and what applies to other cancellations or postponements?
questions.quote: If an Arts in the Open event is cancelled because of bad weather

questions.text: Is event permission needed before the agreement is signed or only before payment, and does the block apply to every instalment? Does the system check the permission's validity, and who verifies it?
questions.quote: shall not be paid until the applicant has uploaded the event permission from the council's events team

questions.text: The spending rule says between November and March without dates, while the approval rule says 1 November to 31 March. Are these the same period, inclusive of both days? Must the system flag or reject activities, costs or payments outside the window, and what happens to a grant spent outside it? Is the 30 April report deadline fixed for all grants, and what happens if it is missed?
questions.quote: Grants must be spent between November and March.

questions.text: The Winter Warmth section does not say whether it is run in rounds or open all year, its funding limits, or who decides. Does the general round set-up and scheme of delegation apply without programme-specific differences?
questions.quote: The Winter Warmth fund supports warm spaces and practical help for residents during the winter months.
